transcript.name: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Alright, let's stop spinning our wheels. We need one clear pitch, one leader. I’ll do it unless someone can convince me they’ll get better results. Otherwise, we’re wasting time.

transcript.name: Erik Lundström
transcript.text: Can we just pause for a second? I think we need to hear from everyone before deciding who leads. Otherwise, we risk missing something important. Thoughts?

transcript.name: Lucía Mendoza
transcript.text: I think it would help to just hear from everyone, even if it's quick. Maybe people have ideas we haven’t heard. I’m okay with someone taking the lead, but I’d like us all to be clear on who’s doing what.

transcript.name: Lilian Njoroge
transcript.text: Maybe we should hear from people who haven’t spoken yet. Sometimes the quiet ideas are the ones that save us. Just saying. Can we get everyone’s quick take?

transcript.name: Wei Zhou
transcript.text: I think it makes sense for us to stick with our usual strengths. If we’re pitching, maybe Marcus leads, but I’d like to double-check the compliance details before we finalize.

transcript.name: Élise Moreau
transcript.text: I think it’s good we’re asking everyone for input, but we really need to decide who’s taking the lead today. Otherwise, we might fall into the same trap as before. Maybe we can hear ideas quickly and vote?

transcript.name: James Thornton
transcript.text: I’ll jump in. If we’re serious about keeping this team, we need to be brutally clear on who’s leading and why. Happy to make my case, but I want to hear concise pitches from anyone interested—right now, no hedging. Let’s not repeat the last mess.

transcript.name: Trang Nguyen
transcript.text: I’m fine with Marcus leading the pitch, as long as we double-check the data set we’re using. Last time there was confusion. I can help review that if needed.

transcript.name: Amitesh Iyer
transcript.text: I don't have a strong preference for who leads, but I think Marcus has handled pitches well before. I can help with the backend details, just let me know what you need from me.

transcript.name: Todd Ramsey
transcript.text: I’m fine with Marcus leading, but we need the technical details locked down this time. I’ll double-check the control system specs before we hand anything over. Don’t want a repeat of last quarter.

transcript.name: Amitesh Iyer
transcript.text: Alright, I’ll focus on backend checks and make sure the APIs are clean before we finalize. Just ping me if anything urgent pops up.

transcript.name: Erik Lundström
transcript.text: Sounds like Marcus will take the lead then. I just want to make sure we keep the backend and compliance checks in the loop—so there aren't any surprises. If anyone sees a gap, say so now or as soon as you spot it. No point in keeping quiet and hoping it works out.

transcript.name: Lucía Mendoza
transcript.text: Just making sure—we’re all clear on who’s doing what, right? If there’s any doubt or someone feels uncomfortable, maybe say so now. I’m fine with Marcus leading and can help with anything HR or onboarding related.

transcript.name: Lilian Njoroge
transcript.text: Alright, I’ll focus on reviewing the data, and if anyone notices a gap or needs support, let me know. I’d rather catch any issues early than scramble later. Sound good?

transcript.name: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Alright, that's it. I’m leading the pitch. If you’ve got concerns or see a hole, speak up now—otherwise, lock in your piece and move. We’re not losing another deal because we hesitated.

transcript.name: Élise Moreau
transcript.text: Okay, I’ll take another look at the user flows to make sure nothing’s missing. If anyone needs a second set of eyes on their section, just let me know.

transcript.name: Wei Zhou
transcript.text: Alright, I’ll double-check the compliance side. If anything looks off, I’ll flag it right away. Let me know if you need a second look at anything.

transcript.name: James Thornton
transcript.text: Quick reminder—if you hit a snag or something doesn't add up, say so straight away. I'd much rather have an awkward interruption now than a crisis later. We can't afford any blind spots.

transcript.name: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: If anyone's confused or holding back, say it now. Otherwise, you know what you’re responsible for. Let’s get this done. I’m not repeating myself again.

transcript.name: James Thornton
transcript.text: Alright, last call—if anyone’s got doubts, let’s hear them now. It’s not a sign of weakness to flag a problem before we’re on the spot. I’d rather be embarrassed here than blindsided in front of leadership.

transcript.name: Amitesh Iyer
transcript.text: No issues from me. I'll keep an eye on the API side, but everything looks set. If anything crops up, I’ll flag it right away.

transcript.name: Élise Moreau
transcript.text: Alright, I’m set on my side. If anything pops up, just shout and I’ll jump in. Otherwise, I’ll keep an eye on the details.
